design: Three-way equal-time comparison of standard direct-rejection BW, reflected-chord BW and unchanged author SCS. All checks use 20 chains per method, one second per chain, one worker, 1500 separate warmup iterations, and 1500x2000 VI draws per map. The two BW methods share one fitted ball map. Every method discards its first third of timed iterations.
protocol_selection: The initial pilot used the existing numerical step ceiling exp(15). Reflected BW reached this ceiling with high acceptance; the pilot is preserved here and was not an independent validation of the final constraint.

After inspecting that pilot, the new comparison was given a common upper step-size bound of 2, the unit ball diameter. This same numerical bound applies to all three methods; it does not imply equal geometric step meanings or that 2 is an optimal choice.
The final checks use fresh sampling seeds 903001 and 904001 with fitting seeds 42 and 43. All three methods and all outcomes are retained.
limitations: Short local checks are exploratory evidence, not full-paper results or a universal performance ranking.
Reflected-chord BW is a new reversible proposal, not literal SCS spherical step-out or specular billiard reflection.

The comparison includes the effect of boundary handling on separately calibrated step sizes. A shared target acceptance need not be attainable for the reflected kernel; ceiling saturation is recorded.
Each check is conditional on its saved ball and sphere fits. Fresh sampling seeds do not undo the pilot-informed choice of the step ceiling.

Original source hashes are preserved exactly as recorded. The reporting footer was updated after final check A; its manifest hashes have not been rewritten to claim that the later reporting text produced that run.

config.tuning_note: All methods retain separate acceptance-target 0.234 calibration. Reflection can make that target unattainable; scale-ceiling saturation is recorded.

initial_ceiling_pilot.target_note: Shared normal-CDF-skewed t target from the DCS experiment. The SCS paper uses a Student-t CDF and nu=1 or2; this applies the SCS kernel with common benchmark tuning to our nu=3 target.

bounded_final_b.target_note: Shared normal-CDF-skewed t target from the DCS experiment. The SCS paper uses a Student-t CDF and nu=1 or2; this applies the SCS kernel with common benchmark tuning to our nu=3 target.
